newsitem.title: CANADA: Falconbridge says Sudbury talks continuing.
newsitem.headline: Falconbridge says Sudbury talks continuing.

text.p: Falconbridge Ltd said on Wednesday it was optimistic the company would reach a new agreement with unionized workers at its Sudbury, Ontario operations before the current contract expired on August 1.
Gerald Foley, Falconbridge's director of human resources, said non-monetary issues were still on the negotiating table. But he added that did not mean talks had fallen behind schedule.
"In terms of timing, I don't believe the timing is off at all. You usually don't get to the money until the end," Foley said in a telephone interview.
"They pay me to be an optimist and I still believe it (an agreement before August 1) will happen," Foley said.
Earlier this month, Falconbridge's 1,400 unionized mine workers in Sudbury voted 91.28 percent in favor of giving their negotiating team a strike mandate.
Falconbridge's Sudbury operations produced 42,100 tonnes of nickel, 48,800 tonnes of copper and 730 tonnes of cobalt last year.
